In a chemistry problem, the choice of the proper root can frequently be made on physical grounds. If x corresponds to a concentration, for example, the negative root is unphysical and can be discarded.

which leads to the roots x  0.00122. We immediately confirm that the solutions obtained in this way are small compared with 2.00 (and 3.00) and that our ap- proximation was a good one. When a quantity (x in this case) is added to or sub- tracted from a larger quantity in a complicated equation, it is usually worthwhile, in solving the equation, to simply neglect the occurrence of the small quantity. Note that this tactic works only for addition and subtraction, never for multiplica- tion or division.
